items.title: Brazilian defender suspended until injured opponent returns to training
items.description: Brazil’s Superior Court of Sports Justice (STJD) has handed Internacional defender Victor Gabriel an unusual suspension, ruling that he cannot play again until Cruzeiro forward Gabriel Pec is medically cleared to resume training following the serious injury he suffered from the defender’s tackle. According to Marca, the decision followed the Sixth Disciplinary Commission’s review of the challenge during Internacional’s 2-1 home defeat to Cruzeiro in a Brazilian Serie A match. The incident occurred 13 minutes into the second half when Victor Gabriel lunged into a challenge on Pec with excessive force. The referee immediately produced a straight red card. Although Pec initially left the pitch with what appeared to be a deep cut to his leg, further medical examinations revealed a fractured left tibia, forcing the striker to undergo surgery. Ordinarily, violent conduct attracts a suspension of between one and six matches. However, the disciplinary panel ruled that such a punishment was inadequate given the severity of the injury. Instead, the court imposed an open-ended suspension, barring Victor Gabriel from playing until Pec returns to full team training. The sanction carries a maximum duration of 180 days. During the disciplinary hearing, an emotional Victor Gabriel apologised for the incident, insisting he never intended to injure his opponent. “I spend sleepless nights praying for him. I sincerely apologise to everyone at Cruzeiro,” the defender told the tribunal. Victor Gabriel is expected to remain sidelined for at least three to four months, based on the estimated recovery period before Pec resumes training. Pec, who joined Cruzeiro from LA Galaxy in July, was making his first start for the Brazilian club when the injury occurred. items.title: Rosatom achève les réacteurs du futur brise-glace nucléaire «Léningrad»
items.description: L'usine de construction mecanique ZiO-Podolsk, filiale de Rosatom situee dans la region de Moscou, a acheve la fabrication du second reacteur RITM-200 destine au brise-glace nucleaire universel « Leningrad ». Cette livraison marque l'achevement de l'ensemble des equipements prevus pour le compartiment reacteur du navire. Pour Alexeï Likhatchov, directeur general de Rosatom, la construction d'un nouveau brise-glace nucleaire constitue toujours un evenement majeur. Le projet « Leningrad » revet toutefois une portee particuliere en raison de son nom, choisi pour rendre hommage a la ville heroïque. Cette decision fait suite a une initiative lancee en 2024 par des veterans et des survivants du siege de Leningrad, a l'occasion du 80e anniversaire de la levee du blocus, puis soutenue par le president russe. Alexeï Likhatchov a rappele que Rosatom avait renoue l'an dernier avec la tradition consistant a attribuer des noms propres a certaines installations nucleaires. Les reacteurs destines au futur brise-glace « Rossiya », dont le nom signifie « Russie », avaient ete baptises « Ilia » et « Dobrynia », en hommage aux bogatyrs, ces heros guerriers legendaires celebres dans les recits epiques russes. Cette annee, apres des echanges avec les veterans et les survivants du siege, les deux reacteurs du « Leningrad » ont recu les noms « Iskra » et « Grom », ces appellations rendant hommage aux operations militaires qui ont permis de rompre le blocus de Leningrad, puis de liberer totalement la ville assiegee en 1944. Pour Alexeï Likhatchov, la portee symbolique de ce projet va de pair avec ses ambitions technologiques. Pendant les quarante prochaines annees, les reacteurs RITM-200 devront fournir l'energie necessaire au fonctionnement du brise-glace le plus puissant au monde. Celui-ci sera charge d'ouvrir la voie dans les glaces epaisses de l'Arctique, d'assurer le passage regulier des navires sur la Route maritime du Nord et de renforcer cette artere logistique essentielle pour la Russie. La fabrication des reacteurs du « Leningrad » ne constitue qu'une etape du vaste programme industriel mene par Rosatom. Treize cuves de petits reacteurs destines a des brise-glaces nucleaires et a des centrales nucleaires de faible puissance se trouvent actuellement a differents stades de fabrication. Parmi elles figurent notamment les equipements prevus pour la centrale nucleaire ouzbeke, dont la construction a ete lancee cette annee. Selon Rosatom, jamais l'industrie nucleaire russe n'avait mene simultanement un programme de fabrication d'une telle ampleur.

items.title: Pakistan welcomes Kuwait's recent ratification of 2023 pact to expand defence cooperation
items.description: Pakistan has welcomed Kuwait’s ratification of a 2023 defence cooperation agreement between the two countries, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday. In a statement responding to media queries, FO spokesperson Dr Tahir Andrabi said the agreement marked “another important milestone in the longstanding defence partnership between the two brotherly countries, dating back to the early 1980s”. “It also reflects the shared resolve of both sides to further strengthen bilateral defence cooperation and elevate their security partnership,” Andrabi was quoted as saying. The statement added that the pact provides a comprehensive institutional framework to broaden defence cooperation, encompassing military training, joint exercises, exchanges of expertise and “other mutually agreed areas of collaboration”. “It will further enhance institutional linkages between the armed forces of both countries and consolidate the longstanding defence ties between Pakistan and Kuwait,” the statement read. The FO added that Pakistan and Kuwait would continue to work closely to implement the pact in accordance with its provisions, thereby “expanding bilateral defence collaboration, strengthening their enduring defence partnership underpinned by mutual trust, shared interests, and close institutional cooperation and contributing to regional peace, security and stability”. The statement came as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a meeting with his Kuwaiti counterpart, Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, in Islamabad earlier today. In a statement, the FO said that DPM Dar welcomed Kuwait’s recent ratification of the agreement, noting that it marked an important milestone in bilateral defence relations and would further strengthen institutional links between both nations’ militaries. The pact was signed on June 11, 2023 at Kuwait’s Ministry of Defence by Ambassador Malik Muhammad Farooq on behalf of Pakistan, and Brigadier General Fawaz Khudair Muhammad Al-Harbi, the ministry’s Joint Planning Director, from the Kuwaiti side, according to the FO. Pakistan has been negotiating an expanded defence pact with Kuwait in exchange for energy cooperation and investment, the Reuters news agency reported earlier this month, citing five sources with knowledge of the talks.

items.title: AJK police accuse JAAC of targeting LEAs, say 26 personnel martyred this year
items.description: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Police on Wednesday said that 26 personnel were martyred this year during incidents of unrest as they accused the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) of deliberately targeting law enforcement agencies (LEAs). Addressing a press conference, AJK police spokesperson and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Riaz Mughal said that members of the proscribed JAAC were “martyring and injuring rangers and police personnel” in AJK. “In 2026 only, 26 of our personnel were martyred, while 157 were seriously injured, and 629 faced minor injuries,” he said, without mentioning the specific incidents in which the casualties occurred. “After this figure, how can you say that they are peaceful protesters?” the SSP asked. The police spokesperson further said, “Our institutions don’t target anyone. We only target those who target our personnel.” The police official’s remarks come after clashes between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot on Monday and Mirpur on Tuesday, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now. “What is happening to police, rangers and other people? They (JAAC members) have held people captive and taken their IDs? Do people not see this?” the SSP said. The police spokesperson suggested that one should go to AJK and impartially witness the situation and the kind of people who were staging sit-ins there. “They have snipers. They target people who are from our institutions and police,” he said, stressing how the JAAC supporters could be called peaceful people who did nothing. SSP Mughal also presented weaponry allegedly recovered from the protesters during different operations. “They use this weapon against law enforcement people.” He recalled that on May 11, 2024, when the police confronted JAAC protesters who were heading towards Muzaffarabad, adding that the incident resulted in the martyrdom of a police officer and 60 personnel getting seriously injured, most of whom were still recovering. At least 174 policemen also sustained minor injuries, the SSP added. SSP Mughal went on to note that in October 2025 , three cops were martyred on the spot, 52 personnel were seriously injured, and 357 others were also hurt. The spokesperson emphasised that these were “anti-state” individuals who were carrying out “terrorist activities” under a plan. Moreover, he claimed that 70 per cent of the protesters were “criminals”, including drug dealers who had taken shelter under the JAAC’s banner. SSP Mughal emphasised that these were “anti-state” people. On Tuesday, the government accused militant elements “pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest. On the other hand, the JAAC alleged that dozens of its supporters were killed in clashes with security personnel, but there was no official confirmation of the claim from any quarters. ‘JAAC working under an agenda’ Earlier in the day, SSP Khawar Ali Shaukat from AJK Police accused the JAAC of working under an “agenda”, saying that sophisticated weapons had been seized from arrested suspects. Senior Superintendent of Police Khawar Ali Shaukat addresses a press conference in Rawlakot on Wednesday. — DawnNewsTV Addressing a press conference, SSP Shaukat alleged that the incidents in Rawalakot had demonstrated that the organisation’s narrative of peaceful protest was inconsistent with events on the ground. “The violent incidents, acts of provocation and attacks on security forces have made the reality clear,” he said, adding that it was the legal and constitutional responsibility of LEAs to act whenever police or other security personnel came under attack. The SSP alleged that armed groups had ambushed officials at different locations across the city over the past two days and opened fire on security personnel with sophisticated weapons. He said one Rangers official was martyred while around 15 police officers and other law enforcement personnel were injured in the attacks. “This demonstrates that the proscribed group is working under an agenda, the purpose of which is to disrupt peace in AJK, disturb the social fabric and damage the atmosphere of brotherhood,” he said. “The events of yesterday and today, the way our forces have been attacked with heavy and sophisticated weapons, show that these groups … this is not an ordinary organisation,” he said. He said law enforcement agencies had arrested several suspects allegedly involved in the violence and recovered a large cache of arms, including heavy weapons. “An automatic American weapon was also recovered,” he said, adding that this indicated that the banned organisation was operating under a “different agenda”. Rejecting what he described as a misleading narrative circulating on social media, Shaukat said the group was falsely portraying itself as peaceful while accusing security forces of targeting protesters. “The facts on the ground are contrary to those claims,” he asserted. He maintained that law enforcement agencies had exercised restraint throughout the situation and only responded when their personnel came under attack.

items.title: Bawumia wishes Black Queens success ahead of CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations opener against Cape Verde

items.title: Diplomatie : Le Mali et le Sénégal réaffirment leur volonté d’agir ensemble face aux défis sécuritaires et économiques
items.description: En visite de travail et de solidarité au Mali, mardi 28 juillet 2026, le président sénégalais, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, a réaffirmé, aux côtés de son homologue malien, le Général d’armée Assimi Goïta, la nécessité pour les deux pays de former un front uni contre les défis sécuritaires et économiques communs. Cette rencontre s’est déroulée sous le signe de la fraternité, du dialogue et de la solidarité. Au-delà de son caractère officiel, cette visite a permis de consolider les relations bilatérales. Les deux chefs d’État ont consacré une large part de leurs échanges aux questions de paix et de sécurité dans le Sahel. Face à une menace terroriste qui ne connaît pas de frontières, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a souligné l’urgence d’une coopération renforcée et d’une action concertée entre les pays de la région. Il a également réaffirmé la disponibilité du Sénégal à accompagner le Mali dans sa lutte contre l’insécurité et dans ses efforts pour la stabilité régionale. Selon la présidence malienne, les discussions ont également porté sur le renforcement de la coopération bilatérale et sur les perspectives de dynamisation des mécanismes régionaux, notamment au sein de l’UEMOA et de l’Organisation pour la mise en valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS). Les deux dirigeants ont convenu de poursuivre les concertations avec leurs homologues en vue de l’organisation, dans les meilleurs délais, d’un sommet des chefs d’État consacré au renforcement de la coopération monétaire et économique, ainsi qu’à la gestion concertée des ressources hydrauliques, précise un compte rendu officiel. items.title: Court blocks Hanan’s wife from travelling to the UK for son’s treatment
items.description: The High Court has dismissed an application by Faiza Seidu-Wuni, seeking permission to travel to the United Kingdom for her son’s medical treatment, ruling that she had failed to demonstrate that the child could not receive the required care in Ghana. The decision means Faiza Seidu-Wuni will remain in the country and continue to comply with the travel restrictions imposed as part of her bail conditions in the ongoing criminal case in which she and her husband, former Chief Executive Officer of the National Food Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO), Abdul Hanan Abdul-Wahab Aludiba, are standing trial. Delivering the ruling, Justice Achibonga held that the application did not establish sufficient grounds to warrant varying the existing bail conditions. The court found that there was no convincing evidence to show that the medical condition cited could not be adequately managed or treated within Ghana’s healthcare system, and consequently dismissed the application. The ruling comes only weeks after Mr Aludiba himself sought the court’s permission to travel abroad on medical grounds, a development that prompted the prosecution to question the timing of the two applications. During earlier proceedings, prosecutors expressed suspicion over the wife’s request, noting that it was filed shortly after her husband had made a similar application. The prosecution argued that the circumstances warranted careful scrutiny, given the pending criminal proceedings against the couple. With Tuesday’s ruling, the travel ban imposed on Mrs Seidu-Wuni remains in force pending the determination of the substantive criminal case. Background Faiza Seidu-Wuni and Mr Aludiba are facing criminal charges in connection with an ongoing prosecution arising from the tenure of Mr Aludiba while at the National Food Buffer Stock Company. Following their arraignment, the court admitted them to bail subject to a number of conditions, including restrictions on international travel without prior judicial approval. Faiza Seidu-Wuni subsequently applied for a temporary variation of those conditions to enable her to accompany her son to the United Kingdom for medical treatment. However, after considering submissions from both the defence and the prosecution, the High Court concluded that the application lacked sufficient medical and evidential basis to justify lifting the travel restrictions. The substantive criminal case against the former NAFCO chief executive and his wife is expected to continue before the High Court.

items.title: Burkina/CSD: le Plan d’action sectoriel de développement de la Gouvernance économique affiche un taux d’exécution physique de 46,92 % à mi-parcours
items.description: BURKINA-MINISTERE-ECONOMIE-FINANCES-CSD Burkina/CSD: le Plan d'action sectoriel de développement de la Gouvernance économique affiche un taux d'exécution physique de 46,92 % à mi-parcours Ouagadougou, 29 juil. 2026 (AIB) – Le ministre de l'Économie et des Finances, Aboubakar Nacanabo, a annoncé mercredi à Ouagadougou que le Plan d'action sectoriel de développement de la Gouvernance économique (PASD-GE) a enregistré, au 30 juin 2026, des taux d'exécution physique et financière de 46,92 % et 23,92 %, respectivement, lors de la revue à mi-parcours 2026 du Cadre sectoriel de dialogue (CSD) « Gouvernance économique ». Selon le ministre, ces performances traduisent une dynamique d'exécution globalement satisfaisante au regard des objectifs fixés, malgré un contexte national et international marqué par de nombreuses contraintes. Il a indiqué que les résultats obtenus reflètent des avancées dans la planification du développement, la gouvernance foncière, la modernisation de l'administration, le renforcement de la transparence et des mécanismes de régulation. Il a noté que cette revue à mi-parcours s'inscrit dans la dynamique du Plan RELANCE 2026-2030, qui place la performance, la redevabilité et l'obtention de résultats concrets au cœur de l'action publique. Sur le plan économique et financier, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo a souligné que le taux de mobilisation des ressources internes s'établit à 58,05 % à fin juin 2026. Il a également relevé que l'opération Diaspora Bonds a permis de mobiliser 151 milliards de FCFA, soit 121,2 % de l'objectif fixé. Le ministre a, en outre, évoqué des acquis, notamment la gestion maîtrisée du marché financier, l'appui renforcé au secteur privé, le développement de la coopération économique et la promotion des investissements, contribuant à la stabilité du système financier national. Il a aussi relevé des progrès au profit des collectivités territoriales à travers des investissements structurants, le renforcement de la résilience des territoires, l'amélioration des infrastructures socioéconomiques et le soutien aux activités productives, en vue d'améliorer les conditions de vie des populations. Pour le ministre Nacanabo, ces acquis démontrent que, malgré un environnement national et international marqué par de multiples contraintes, le secteur de l'économie et des finances demeure mobilisé pour traduire les orientations du Gouvernement en résultats concrets au bénéfice des concitoyens. « Ces acquis constituent un encouragement à poursuivre les réformes avec davantage de rigueur, de célérité et d'innovation afin d'atteindre les ambitions du Plan RELANCE », a-t-il exhorté. Il ressort des échanges qui ont suivi la présentation du rapport de performance du Plan d'action sectoriel de développement de la Gouvernance économique à fin juin 2026 que les résultats sont globalement satisfaisants, mais que des efforts restent à fournir. Agence d'information du Burkina BAK/yos

items.title: Trump administration bans new Chinese humanoid robots
items.description: The Trump administration on Tuesday announced a ban on new foreign-made humanoid robot imports to the US over “unacceptable risks” to America’s national security. The move applies to advanced robots – including humanoid and four-legged machines. Many of them are made in China, which is competing with the US to develop robotics and artificial intelligence (AI). The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) also banned imports of power inverters – devices used in data centres and solar panels – which it said could also pose a risk to the US economy. The Chinese embassy in Washington said Beijing has long opposed the US’ “politicising” of trade issues and sanctions based on “groundless pretexts”. FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the agency was doing its part “to secure America’s critical supply chains”. The FCC has added the items to its Covered List – a register of goods and services that are deemed a risk to US national security. The ban applies to new foreign-produced advanced robotic devices and power inverters and does not prevent the sale or import of any existing models that had been previously authorised by the FCC. The FCC cited concerns that the use of foreign-made inverters could allow overseas firms to turn them off, steal data, facilitate remote access and surveillance by “foreign government actors, or be otherwise exploited through a cyberattack”. It added that the use of robots made outside the US could allow “malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services, or to remotely commandeer the robots”. The Chinese embassy in Washington also said Beijing will “take all necessary measures” in response to any moves that harm its interests, urging all countries to work together to develop AI “for the positive and for good”. It called on the US to “abandon its hegemonic mindset, and stop smearing Chinese companies and threatening them with sanctions”. The BBC has contacted major Chinese robot manufacturers Unitree, UBTech and AgiBot for comment. China’s exports have come under intense scrutiny by the US as the Trump administration attempts to address trade imbalances with the world’s second largest economy. Despite being the world’s biggest exporter of electric vehicles, China has been effectively shut out of the American market by a steep tariff. Washington has also blocked the sale of cutting-edge US semiconductors to China in a bid to protect national security, slow Beijing’s military modernisation and maintain America’s lead in AI. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also warned that Chinese AI firms could face sanctions over allegations that they have stolen American intellectual property. In response the Chinese government has said its country’s development of AI was “the result of its own dedication and effort as well as international cooperation”. The US will be keen to avoid a repeat of the squeeze on supply chains that was triggered last year when China tightened export controls on rare earths – critical for electronics. Chinese technology firms have rapidly developed humanoid robots to be used in settings including factories and homes. Companies have also been quick to market their machines to businesses and the public ahead of US humanoid robot rivals like Elon Musk’s Tesla and Boston Dynamics.

Cette opération a permis de prendre pour cible deux véhicules tout-terrain armés ainsi qu'un groupe de combattants appartenant à une coalition regroupant le groupe « Soutien de l'islam et des musulmans » et le **Front de libération de l'Azawad**. L’armée malienne a affirmé que ses forces continueraient les opérations de surveillance et de sécurisation dans différentes régions du pays, dans le cadre de ses efforts visant à traquer les groupes armés et à renforcer son contrôle sur les zones où les militants sont actifs.

items.title: Japon : que nous dit la tentative d’ouverture d’un débat publique sur le nucléaire par l’actuel ministre de la Défense ?
items.description: À télécharger Lire la note (PDF) En dépit du traumatisme de Hiroshima et de Nagasaki et d’un pacifisme institutionnel ancré dans la constitution de 1947, le Japon a vu régulièrement resurgir la question du nucléaire militaire. Le durcissement de son environnement régional avec la nucléarisation de la Corée du Nord, les tensions grandissantes avec la Chine et une Russie belliciste semblent avoir créé les conditions d’un réexamen des principes de la politique nucléaire japonaise pour le gouvernement Takaichi. Le débat traditionnel sur la question a jusqu’ici été structuré autour de trois thématiques : le partage nucléaire avec les États-Unis, le maintien d’une dissuasion crédible face à des voisins révisionnistes et plus épisodiquement sur l’intérêt pour le Japon de posséder ses propres armes nucléaires. Les discussions les plus récentes, généralement prudentes et circonscrites à de rares déclarations de responsables politiques, dont les anciens Premiers ministres Shinzō Abe et Shigeru Ishiba, ont moins porté sur la perspective d’une nucléarisation du Japon que sur l’intérêt de réfléchir sur les options nucléaires dont disposerait le pays en cas de crise alors que son voisinage est perçu comme de plus en plus menaçant. Aussi, les propos de Shinjirō Koizumi, actuel ministre de la Défense, sur le fait que le nucléaire constituait pour le Japon « un sujet que nous ne pouvons pas éviter » n’ont pas manqué d’attirer l’attention. Comment les interpréter et que peuvent-ils révéler des intentions de l’actuel gouvernement très en pointe sur les questions de défense ? S’agit-il de préparer l’opinion publique japonaise et internationale à de nouvelles avancées sécuritaires de l’archipel ? En effet ces déclarations interviennent alors qu’une réflexion est engagée depuis de longs mois sur la mise à jour des principaux documents relatifs à la défense du pays publiés en 2022 et qui ont été perçus comme un tournant stratégique majeur. L’article Japon : que nous dit la tentative d’ouverture d’un débat publique sur le nucléaire par l’actuel ministre de la Défense ? est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Guinée: « je suis parti avec des convictions, je reviens avec une mission», Béa Diallo ministre de la Jeunesse
items.description: Ce mercredi 29 juillet 2026, dans les locaux du ministère à Kaloum, la cérémonie de passation de service entre Cellou Baldé et Lansana Béa Diallo a dépassé le simple protocole administratif. Elle a marqué le retour de deux départements distincts, chacun appelé à relever ses propres défis : la Jeunesse d'un côté, les Sports de l'autre. Quelques jours après le décret présidentiel mettant fin à la fusion du ministère de la Jeunesse et des Sports, les deux responsables ont officiellement pris possession de leurs nouveaux portefeuilles sous la présidence du ministre Secrétaire général du Gouvernement, Tamba Benoît Kamano, en présence de plusieurs membres du gouvernement, des cadres de l'administration, des acteurs du sport, des organisations de jeunesse et des familles. Au moment de quitter la gestion de la Jeunesse pour se consacrer exclusivement aux Sports, Cellou Baldé a choisi de regarder le chemin parcouru avant d'évoquer celui qui reste à accomplir. Sans triomphalisme, il a rappelé les réformes engagées en faveur de l’emploi des jeunes, du volontariat, de la formation professionnelle, de l'entrepreneuriat et de la réalisation d'infrastructures destinées à accompagner leur épanouissement. Pour lui, la décision de créer deux ministères distincts constitue un choix stratégique : « La décision de scinder le ministère traduit une volonté politique forte de renforcer l'efficacité de l'action publique en accordant à la jeunesse et au sport toute l'attention stratégique qu'ils méritent . » Désormais à la tête du ministère des Sports, Cellou Baldé a aussitôt fixé le cap. Il a invité les acteurs du monde sportif à tourner la page des rivalités pour construire une vision commune. « Aucun pays ne bâtit une grande nation sportive dans la division. Ensemble, faisons du sport guinéen un secteur fort, crédible et capable de porter haut les couleurs de notre pays », ajoute-t-il. Face à lui, Lansana Béa Diallo retrouvait un ministère qu'il avait quitté il y a près de deux ans. Son retour n'avait rien d'un simple recommencement. Dans sondiscours, l'ancien champion de boxe a expliqué revenir avec une expérience nouvelle et une conviction intacte : celle de poursuivre une œuvre qu'il estime inachevée. « Je suis venu avec une vision, je suis parti avec des convictions, je reviens avec une mission : achever avec vous ce que nous avons commencé ensemble. Le temps de la découverte est terminé, le temps des résultats commence », prévient-il. Tout au long de son intervention, le nouveau ministre de la Jeunesse a recentré son message sur ce qu'il considère comme la véritable richesse du pays : les jeunes. Pour lui, l'enjeu dépasse la gestion d'une administration. Il s'agit de redonner confiance à une génération souvent confrontée au chômage, au doute et à l'exil. « Mon rêve est qu'un jeune Guinéen ne quitte plus son pays parce qu'il n'y voit plus son avenir. Je veux qu'il choisisse de rester parce qu'il y trouvera des opportunités, un emploi, un projet à bâtir et une vie digne à construire », conclut-il.

items.title: Ghana Publishing Company acquires rare six-colour digital press to boost commercial printing
items.description: The Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL) has acquired a rare six-colour Xerox Iridesse digital press as part of efforts to strengthen its commercial printing operations and position itself as a leading player in Ghana’s printing industry. Managing Director Nana Kwasi Boatey Esq. described the acquisition as a major milestone in the company’s transformation agenda, saying the new equipment will enable GPCL to deliver premium-quality printing services while competing more effectively with private sector operators. According to him, the Xerox Iridesse press offers capabilities beyond conventional digital printing machines commonly used in Ghana. “Ordinarily, most of the digital presses in Ghana are four-colour machines. You have the four basic colours, which are yellow, magenta, cyan and black. But this is a six colour. It’s able to give you two additional colours at any time,” Mr Boatey said. He explained that the additional colour stations allow the machine to produce speciality finishes, including metallic gold and silver, white, pink and other premium print effects that are increasingly sought after in the commercial printing market. Mr Boatey said only three other machines with similar capabilities were available in Ghana at the time of the acquisition, giving the state-owned company a competitive advantage. The Managing Director said the investment reflects GPCL’s commitment to becoming a modern and commercially competitive printing company. “You see, the Ghana Publishing Company is into the commercial printing business. And we want to be able to compete favourably in the commercial market,” he said. He added that the acquisition fulfilled the company’s pledge to improve its production capacity and service delivery. “I say without doubt or authority that if you want the best quality press—digital printing of any sort—with the acquisition of this Iridesse SC1000 machine, the best place to go will be the Ghana Publishing Company. Just come and see the output and decide for yourself,” he stated. The investment follows GPCL’s strongest financial performance in recent years. The company recorded a profit after tax of GH¢16.96 million in the 2025 financial year, up from GH¢2.23 million in 2024, while total revenue increased from GH¢60.78 million to GH¢72.85 million. Responding to concerns about the cost of the investment, Mr Boatey said the company’s improved financial position made it possible to invest in strategic assets that would generate long-term value. “What is the point in having liquidity if you’re not investing in the company? The company has needs. If the company has some liquidity that has to be disposed of in any way, this is the best way to do it,” he said. The acquisition forms part of a broader restructuring programme introduced since Mr Boatey’s appointment in February 2025. The reforms include the introduction of a two-shift working system aligned with the government’s 24-hour economy policy, the creation of new operational departments and the rollout of a security-enhanced gazette. “We believe that with this as an addition to the already significant gamut of equipment that we have, we should be able to compete very favourably in the market,” Mr Boatey said. “What we desire is to build a Ghana Publishing Company that will be an ultramodern publishing company in the West African subregion.” GPCL said the machine has already been delivered, with installation and staff training currently underway ahead of full commercial operations. The company also indicated that it intends to continue investing in modern equipment as it expands its footprint within Ghana and across the West African sub-region.

items.title: Incendies en Tunisie : près de 12 000 hectares de forêts détruits depuis le début de l’été
items.description: La deuxieme moitie du mois de juillet a marque un tournant dans la saison des incendies en Tunisie. Selon les donnees communiquees le 29 juillet 2026 par la Direction generale des forets, pres de 12 000 hectares de couvert forestier ont ete detruits entre le 10 et le 26 juillet. Le Kef, Beja, Jendouba et Bizerte comptent parmi les gouvernorats les plus touches. Le 23 juillet, un premier bilan faisait encore etat de six incendies majeurs ayant ravage plus de 4 000 hectares en moins de quinze jours. Plusieurs foyers restaient alors actifs, notamment a Takrouna, dans le gouvernorat du Kef, et a Cap Negro, dans celui de Beja. Le bilan a ensuite ete revu a la hausse, a mesure que les incendies se poursuivaient et que les superficies sinistrees etaient evaluees. Avant le 10 juillet, pres de 900 interventions avaient deja ete recensees. Elles concernaient principalement des feux dans des cultures cerealieres, sans pertes forestieres importantes. La situation a brusquement change avec l'apparition de foyers majeurs dans des zones montagneuses difficiles d'acces. Des equipes confrontees au manque de moyens La Tunisie ne dispose que de 260 agents forestiers pour surveiller pres d'un million d'hectares, alors que les besoins sont estimes a environ mille agents. Au plus fort de la crise, certains d'entre eux sont restes mobilises pendant 48 a 72 heures sans veritable releve. a ce deficit d'effectifs s'ajoute le manque d'equipements adaptes. Les responsables forestiers reclament notamment le renouvellement des camions, le renforcement des engins lourds et une meilleure repartition du materiel entre les gouvernorats. Chaque region doit pouvoir intervenir rapidement, sans dependre systematiquement de renforts venus d'autres parties du pays. Les fortes temperatures ne sont pas directement a l'origine des incendies, mais elles accelerent leur propagation. Selon un responsable de la Direction generale des forets, pres de 95 % des departs de feu sont lies a l'activite humaine, qu'il s'agisse d'imprudences, de brûlages agricoles ou d'actes volontaires. Plusieurs personnes ont ete interpellees et des procedures judiciaires sont en cours. Pour maîtriser plusieurs foyers majeurs, la Tunisie a egalement beneficie d'un soutien aerien fourni par l'Algerie et l'Italie. Des consequences durables pour les regions touchees Les degâts se mesureront sur plusieurs decennies. Une foret a besoin d'environ trente ans pour retrouver son equilibre ecologique. Dans certains cas, la reconstitution complete de la vegetation, de la faune et des interactions naturelles peut prendre entre 70 et 80 ans. Les incendies menacent aussi les activites economiques locales. Dans plusieurs zones forestieres, des familles dependent de la collecte des plantes aromatiques, des ressources naturelles et des petites activites developpees autour de ces espaces. Greenpeace Moyen-Orient et Afrique du Nord estime que les incendies enregistres au Maghreb traduisent une aggravation des risques climatiques. Selon l'organisation, le changement climatique ne provoque pas directement les departs de feu, mais peut favoriser leur propagation et renforcer leur intensite. Parallelement aux operations menees sur le terrain, la Tunisie a recu plusieurs marques de solidarite regionale. Lors d'un entretien telephonique avec Kaïs Saïed le 28 juillet, le president egyptien Abdel Fattah al-Sissi a propose l'aide du Caire face aux incendies. Le chef de l'etat tunisien a presente les efforts engages pour proteger les citoyens et les biens publics, tout en remerciant l'egypte pour son soutien.

Plateau Assembly withdraws controversial ex-lawmakers’ pension bill
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – The Plateau State House of Assembly has bowed to mounting public pressure and withdrawn the controversial Bill seeking to provide pension allowances for former members, principal officers and presiding officers of the Assembly. The decision followed widespread condemnation by organised labour, civil society organisations, and members of the public, who argued that the proposed legislation was ill-timed in view of the prevailing economic hardship and the plight of workers and pensioners in the state. Announcing the withdrawal of the bill on Thursday in Jos, the Majority Leader of the House and Chairman of the Joint Committee on Rules and Business, Finance and House Services, Hon. Joseph G. Gokum, said the action was taken after extensive consultations, public feedback and careful deliberations by the committee. Gokum said the 10th Plateau State House of Assembly remained committed to transparency, accountability and people-centred legislation, stressing that lawmakers had listened to the concerns expressed by citizens and other critical stakeholders. According to him, since the introduction of the bill, the Assembly had received submissions from Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), labour unions and concerned Plateau citizens, whose views reflected the current economic realities and the expectations of the people. “We acknowledge and respect the position of our stakeholders. Their voices reflect the realities of our time and the expectations of the people we serve. “As representatives of the people, it is our duty to ensure that every law we make promotes equity, fairness and the overall welfare of all Plateau citizens, especially workers and pensioners who have given years of service to the state,” he said. He explained that after due deliberation, the Joint Committee unanimously resolved to withdraw the bill. According to the Majority Leader, the decision should not be interpreted as a sign of weakness but as evidence that the Assembly respects democratic principles and public opinion. “The decision is a demonstration of maturity, humility and respect for public opinion. Democracy is strengthened when leaders listen to the people and act in their best interest,” he stated. The statement announcing the withdrawal was jointly signed by Gokum; Chairman, House Committee on House Services and Welfare, Hon. Ibrahim Galadima; and Chairman, House Committee on Finance, Hon. Eli Ankala Bako. The development comes barely 24 hours after members of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Trade Union Congress (TUC), civil society organisations and other concerned citizens staged a protest at the Plateau State House of Assembly, demanding the immediate withdrawal of the bill. The protesters had described the proposed pension package for former lawmakers as insensitive, arguing that it came at a time many workers and retirees were struggling with economic hardship and unpaid entitlements. Gokum thanked the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), the Trade Union Congress (TUC), Civil Society Organisations and other stakeholders for engaging the Assembly peacefully and constructively on the issue. “On behalf of the Joint Committee and the entire House, we sincerely appreciate the Civil Society Organisations, Labour Unions and all Plateau citizens who constructively engaged with us on this matter. Your vigilance strengthens our democracy,” he added. He reaffirmed that the Plateau State House of Assembly, under the leadership of the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Naanlong Daniel, would continue to enact laws aimed at promoting good governance, accountability, unity and sustainable development across the state. The post Plateau Assembly withdraws controversial ex-lawmakers’ pension bill appeared first on Vanguard News .

Affaire Djiba Diané : relaxé, il récupère sa Range Rover, le tribunal déboute Kanis Diané, représentée par son père, Madifing Diané
items.description: Le tribunal de première instance de Dixinn a rendu son verdict ce mercredi 29 juillet 2026 dans l’affaire opposant Djiba Diané à Kanis Komara Diané, représentée par son père, Elhadj Madifing Diané. Poursuivi pour abus de confiance ainsi que pour faux et usage de faux, Djiba Diané a été déclaré non coupable et renvoyé des fins de la poursuite. Présidée par le juge Mohamed Sangaré, la juridiction a estimé que les faits reprochés à Djiba Diané n’étaient pas établis. Elle l’a en conséquence relaxé et a ordonné la restitution du véhicule de marque Range Rover, au cœur du litige. Cette décision conforte la thèse de la défense qui, tout au long de la procédure, a soutenu que son client était le propriétaire légitime du véhicule. Lors de ses réquisitions, le procureur de la République, Mamadou Yaya Fatoumata Boiro, avait indiqué ne pas disposer de preuves suffisantes pour soutenir les poursuites. Il n’avait ainsi requis ni la condamnation ni la relaxe de Djiba Diané, préférant laisser au tribunal le soin d’apprécier les éléments du dossier et de statuer. Pour sa part, la partie civile, qui revendiquait également la propriété de la Range Rover, avait demandé la restitution du véhicule. Son avocat avait en outre sollicité la condamnation de Djiba Diané au paiement de 100 millions de francs guinéens à titre de dommages et intérêts. Avec ce jugement, le tribunal met un terme, en première instance, à cette procédure en donnant gain de cause à Djiba Diané. Lébêré Baldé L’article Affaire Djiba Diané : relaxé, il récupère sa Range Rover, le tribunal déboute Kanis Diané, représentée par son père, Madifing Diané est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Une délégation omanaise en visite en Mauritanie pour renforcer la coopération numérique entre les deux pays
items.description: Une délégation gouvernementale omanaise a entamé hier une visite en Mauritanie afin de mener des entretiens avec des responsables gouvernementaux et des acteurs du secteur privé sur le renforcement de la coopération en matière de transition numérique et l'exploration d'opportunités d'investissement dans les secteurs des technologies et des télécommunications, alors que Nouakchott s'efforce d'accélérer la mise en œuvre de programmes de modernisation de l'administration et de l'économie numérique. La délégation est présidée par Ali bin Amer Al-Shidani, secrétaire d’État au ministère omanais des Transports, des Télécommunications et des Technologies de l’information, et comprend des responsables, des experts et des représentants d’entreprises spécialisées dans les télécommunications, l’intelligence artificielle, les centres de données et l’entrepreneuriat. À son arrivée à Nouakchott, la délégation a été accueillie par Khaled Abidine Sidi, secrétaire général du ministère de la Transformation numérique et de la Modernisation de l’administration. Selon le ministère de la Transformation numérique, la visite se poursuivra jusqu’au 30 juillet et prévoit des discussions sur l’échange d’expériences dans les domaines de l’administration numérique, de l’économie numérique, de l’intelligence artificielle, de la cybersécurité et des centres de données, ainsi que l’étude de programmes de formation des talents et de soutien à l’innovation et à l’entrepreneuriat. Le programme de la visite prévoit également l’organisation d’un forum d’affaires mauritano-omanais sur la numérisation, qui réunira des entreprises des deux pays afin d’étudier les opportunités d’investissement et de nouer des partenariats dans les domaines des télécommunications, des technologies et des services numériques, ainsi que des rencontres professionnelles et des visites sur le terrain d’institutions et d’installations opérant dans le secteur numérique.

However, the APC had issued a statement through the Campaign Council spokesperson, Remi Omowaye, alleging that the Accord is sponsoring a protest to disrupt the INEC’s stakeholders meeting. items.title: Osun Election: Tension as INEC holds stakeholders’ meeting ahead of governorship poll
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo There was tension on Wednesday at the venue of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) stakeholders’ meeting in Osun State ahead of the August 15, 2026 governorship election. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, had arrived in the state on Tuesday and paid courtesy visits to the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, and other traditional rulers. However, the stakeholders’ meeting, held at Atlantis Hall and attended by political parties, civil society organisations (CSOs) and other stakeholders, was disrupted by intermittent exchanges between supporters of the Accord Party and the All Progressives Congress (APC). The meeting began peacefully but became rowdy when the Osun State Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Gotan, was invited to address participants. While some attendees applauded his remarks, others booed, creating a noisy atmosphere that made it difficult for participants to follow his speech. A similar situation occurred when the Chairman of the Imole Campaign Council Media Directorate, Hon. Bamidele Salam, attempted to speak, as some participants also interrupted his remarks. Outside the venue, a group of protesters, mainly women, staged a peaceful demonstration, calling for a credible governorship election. They carried placards with inscriptions including, “We want peace in Osun, not war” and “Osun election must be free and fair.” Meanwhile, the APC Campaign Council, through its spokesperson, Remi Omowaye, alleged that the protest was sponsored by the Accord Party to disrupt the stakeholders’ meeting. Security was reinforced around the venue, with armed security personnel deployed both within and outside the hall to maintain order. items.title: NDC welcomes Supreme Court ruling on political party delegate system, says it is ready to comply
items.description: The governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) has welcomed the Supreme Court’s ruling declaring Ghana’s political party delegate system unconstitutional, describing the decision as fair and one the party is well-prepared to implement. According to the party’s Deputy Director of IT and Elections, Rashid Tanko Computer, the NDC has no reservations about the landmark judgment and already possesses the membership data and organisational structures required to transition to a more inclusive electoral system. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Wednesday, July 29, Mr Tanko said the party had experimented with a similar model more than a decade ago, giving it valuable experience in broadening participation in internal elections. “As a party, the NDC, for us, we consider it to be fair. We don’t have any issues with it,” he said. He explained that between 2014 and 2015, the NDC piloted a system that enabled a wider section of its membership to participate in selecting parliamentary candidates. The exercise relied on biometric technology, with printed registration booklets distributed across the regions to capture members’ details and compile a voters’ register. Although the initiative encountered logistical challenges, Mr Tanko said the objective was to decentralise the party’s internal electoral process and allow all members to participate in choosing parliamentary candidates. “We actually wanted to decentralise and make sure that all our membership would participate in the voting of our candidate. The NDC has been in the forefront of this kind of system, although we later suspended it,” he noted. Mr Tanko further disclosed that the party had, even before the court’s ruling, begun strengthening its membership database in anticipation of a future shift towards universal participation in internal elections. He said the NDC reopened its membership register in February this year to enrol and digitally capture members across the country. The updated register was subsequently used to conduct the party’s branch elections, which concluded last week. “So for now, at the NDC, we are okay with it. We are fine with it. We have our data. To implement the decision of the Supreme Court will not be a difficult one for us,” he stressed. The Supreme Court’s ruling is expected to significantly alter the internal electoral processes of political parties by requiring them to adopt systems that allow broader participation by their members, replacing the long-standing delegate system used to elect parliamentary and presidential candidates.

items.title: Kozah /santé : La population de la Kara dépistée aux hépatites virales
items.description: Kara, 29 juil. (ATOP) – Des séances de sensibilisation couplées de dépistage gratuit aux hépatites virales ont été initiées les 28 et 29 juillet au Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) de Kara en faveur de la population de la région. Cette opération est à l’actif de la Société togolaise d’hépato-gastro entérologie et d’endoscopie digestive (SOTOGEED), section Kara. Elle intervient dans le cadre de la journée mondiale de lutte contre les hépatites virales (A, B, C, D et E) observée chaque 28 juillet. Les séances visent à sensibiliser la population aux risques liés à ces infections virales, à promouvoir le dépistage précoce, la vaccination et à orienter d’éventuelles personnes infectées vers une prise en charge spécialisée pour un traitement efficace. Il s’agit aussi de répondre à la nécessité de détecter précocement des maladies qui évoluent souvent sans symptômes afin de mettre la population à l’abri d’éventuelles infections inhérentes et favoriser l’accès au traitement pour ceux qui seront déclarés positifs. Phase d’entretien avec les participants avant le dépistage Les participants ont été sensibilisés sur les différentes sortes d’hépatites virales, notamment B et C qui sont fréquemment rencontrées. Ils ont aussi bénéficié des tests de dépistage gratuit. Environ 750 personnes ont été touchées par cette activité. Celles qui sont déclarées négatives, ont été édifiées sur les mesures de prévention et orientées vers les services de vaccination afin de se prémunir. Quant à celles dont les résultats sont positifs, elles ont été référées au service spécialisé du CHU pour des examens complémentaires approfondis et un suivi médical adéquat. Le médecin hépato-gastro-entérologue au CHU Kara et membre de la SOTOGEED, Dr. El Hadj Yakoubou Rafiou a indiqué que les hépatites virales sont des maladies qui tuent silencieusement. « Elles ne donnent généralement aucun signe au début. Ce n’est qu’au stade des complications, notamment la cirrhose du foie, que les patients consultent, avec un gonflement du ventre et des membres inférieurs », a-t-il expliqué. Selon lui, le dépistage constitue le moyen le plus efficace pour connaître son statut et d’éviter les complications, précisant que les tests de dépistage, coûtent chers. Dr. Yakoubou Rafiou a profité pour exhorter la population à se faire vacciner contre l’hépatite B si les examens sont révélés négatifs, soulignant que la vaccination demeure le seul moyen efficace de prévention contre cette maladie. ATOP/AE/TAL/SED/BV

items.title: Re-polling demand, Form-47 jibe and doomsday talk — PPP, PML-N continue to trade barbs over Mirpur election results
items.description: PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari continued his tirade against the PML-N — an ally of his party in the Centre — on Wednesday, reiterating his allegations in the first phase of Azad Jammu and Kashmir elections and demanding re-polling. Addressing a PPP workers’ convention in Muzaffarabad, he called on the Election Commission to hold re-polling in Mirpur if “you are not involved in this rigging”. Directly taking a jibe at Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, he said: “If someone is sitting on the PM’s seat, or someone is sitting on the CM’s position today, even a child knows that it is not because of the people’s votes or your performance but because of Form-47.” Form-47 is the provisional consolidated statement of results of the vote count of all polling stations in a constituency, prepared by the returning officer (RO) concerned. The term has also been used mainly by the opposition PTI since the 2024 general elections in the country to allege rigging in the polls. Elections in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, and the PML-N won nine out of a total 13 seats up for grabs in the first phase in Mirpur. Bilawal’s allegations on Wednesday were in continuation of his party’s accusations from the day before, when the PPP and the PML-N traded barbs over election results, with Maryam saying in a televised address that it was “not the state that decides election results, but the people”. She also urged the PPP to accept defeat. Shortly before Bilawal’s speech on Wednesday, she, too, took a jibe at the PPP on X, saying: “The PPP, which is the master of the fine art of rigging, is crying foul. When’s the doomsday?” Responding to her on X, PPP’s Sharjeel Memon said, “This is not you speaking but Form-47. Doomsday came in 2024, when mandates were being distributed in charity.” Meanwhile, the AJK Election Commission officially notified the return of the 13 successful candidates elected from Mirpur division in the first phase of the Legislative Assembly elections held on July 27. According to a press release on the notifications, the PML-N secured nine of the 13 seats, while the PPP won the remaining four. The notified winners were: LA-1 (Mirpur-I): Chaudhry Azhar Sadiq (PML-N) LA-2 (Mirpur-II): Chaudhry Qasim Majeed (PPP) LA-3 (Mirpur-III): Chaudhry Yasir Sultan (PPP) LA-4 (Mirpur-IV): Rukhsar Ahmed (PML-N) LA-5 (Bhimber-I): Waqar Ahmed Noor (PML-N) LA-6 (Bhimber-II): Mohammad Razzaq Chaudhry (PML-N) LA-7 (Bhimber-III): Chaudhry Tariq Farooq (PML-N) LA-8 (Kotli-I): Zafar Iqbal Malik (PPP) LA-9 (Kotli-II): Umair Naeem (PML-N) LA-10 (Kotli-III): Mohammad Yasin Chaudhry (PPP) LA-11 (Kotli-IV): Mohammad Asif (PML-N) LA-12 (Kotli-V): Mohammad Riasat Khan (PML-N) LA-13 (Kotli-VI): Raja Ayaz Ahmed (PML-N) The notification was issued on the basis of the official results submitted by the respective returning officers (ROs) after the completion of polling and counting in the first phase of the three-stage AJK elections, a spokesperson for the commission said. ‘Product of rigging’ For his part, Bilawal assailed the PML-N, claiming that the party was a “product of rigging”. Drawing a contrast with his own party, Bilawal said that the PPP’s track record “dated back three generations”. He went on to claim that “there has not been a single election where the PML-N has won through the people’s vote […], but always due to rigging”. “Do they think we will allow them to rig the elections in Kashmir?” Bilawal asked rhetorically. “The Kashmiri people will not bow down and let anyone steal their mandate,” he added. “This is Muzaffarabad, not Srinagar,” the PPP chairman said, vowing that his party would ensure that the opposing side’s “rigging attempts go in vain”. Speaking about Monday’s elections, Bilawal wondered how PPP candidate Chaudhry Yasin could have lost given his performance in the previous election. “In General Faiz’s era, when Chaudhry Yasin won both the seats he was contesting despite his sons being imprisoned, and shots fired at him, then how can I accept the results in this election?” Bilawal claimed that Yasin’s win was “turned into a defeat” when the PML-N seized Mirpur’s 30 polling stations, for which Bilawal claimed he had “video evidence”. He further claimed that the voter turnout at the 30 polling stations was 90 per cent while in most constituencies the turnout was hardly 40-50pc. The PPP chairman promised his party’sworkers that he will “take back every single stolen vote”. He said he was ready to accept defeat but added that “if you are going to steal our mandate by rigging the election, then I cannot accept these results”. Bilawal also reiterated PPP’s recommendation regarding the formation of a truth and reconciliation commission to address the ongoing unrest in AJK. “I am not presenting this proposal on behalf of the state or the protesters, but on behalf of every Kashmiri who does not belong to either.” He called on both sides — the government and the now proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee — to accept the demand. “If you walk the righteous path and if you are on the side of the truth, then why are you not forming the commission?” he asked. Bilawal asked the crowd to vote for the PPP in the upcoming phase of the election on August 2, stating: “Convey the message to Poonch, Rawalakot and Islamabad that Muzaffarabad demands a truth and reconciliation commission be formed.” The PPP chairman stressed that he wanted to ensure for the people of Kashmir “the right to governance and the right to employment” but held that he would not do so by locking down the city. Instead, he said he would do so by gaining power through the electoral process. He assured the crowd that he would ensure AJK’s representation in Islamabad and at forums such as the National Finance Commission (NFC) and the Council of Common Interests (CCI). Bilawal further stated that when PPP spoke of employment in the region, it did so because the leadership was cognisant of the “economic crisis” in AJK. He then again took a jibe at PML-N, whose economic philosophy, Bilawal claimed, was guided by the principle that “the rich should get richer”. “They taunt us and tell us that we want to turn Kashmir into Sindh. No, I want Kashmir to stay Kashmir and let the people decide its fate,” Bilawal said. “Punjab, Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh or Balochistan cannot decide Kashmir’s future.” ‘Commission’s role exposed’ Addressing a press conference in Lahore on Wednesday, PPP Central Punjab General Secretary Hassan Murtaza claimed that the rigging had “exposed the commission’s role and the robbery of the PPP’s mandate in broad daylight”. He alleged that “such rigging had never been seen before in Pakistan”. “In Charhoi, from where Chaudhry Yasin was contesting, 30 polling stations were held hostage, and when the polling time ended, polling agents were not allowed to sit together,” he claimed. Murtaza added that in Javed Badhanvi’s constituency, similar tactics were employed. “And on the day of polling, our worker Mukhtar Younis was martyred,” he said. He added that polling stations in Chaudhry Ikhlaq’s constituency were also taken hostage, and so were those in Chaudhry Pervaiz Ashraf’s constituency, where Murtaza claimed he was in “close competition”. Murtaza alleged that holding the elections in phases was done to “enable rigging”. Speaking about the role of the AJK Election Commission, the PPP leader likened its role to that of Punjab’s Crime Control Department. “It was deciding who is to be half-fried and full fried, whose polling agents to pick and what polling stations to seize,” he said, adding that “extending the voting time by one hour was done so they could get time to stamp votes for the PML-N”. “The AJK Election Commission played the role of a commissioned agent,” he remarked. He said that PPP leaders brought the issue to the commission’s attention and had urged it not to facilitate rigging. “We kept telling you that buses were being given away and the code of conduct was being violated and you only took notice when the whole of social media assailed you for it,” he said. He recalled that a day earlier, CM Maryam made a statement over “how the PPP had nothing to show for itself”. At this, he said: “The past is witness that it was the PPP who got AJK the right to engage in parliamentary politics.” He added that during the PPP’s six months in power in AJK, the region’s then-premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore had accepted 35 of the demands of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) “with one executive order”. However, he noted that there were two demands where the “federal government was involved or it required constitutional amendments”. He said that PPP leaders Raja Pervaiz Ashraf and Qamar Zaman Qaira were part of the negotiating team that “begged the protesters for two weeks so all stakeholders may be brought on board, but the group did not accept the request”. However, he held that JAAC’s refusal did not mean that the state should end the negotiating process altogether and the PPP’s proposal for a truth and reconciliation commission be dismissed. “If the state had shown some flexibility, the issue could have been resolved,” he added. The PPP has repeatedly called for the establishment of a truth and reconciliation commission amid protests in AJK. Over the past month, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues — most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly reserved for refugees from Indian-occupied Jammu and Kashmir who settled in mainland Pakistan after 1947, which has resulted in protests across the region. Ashraf calls for probe Separately, PPP’s Ashraf addressed a press conference in Islamabad, where he presented what he described as evidence for the alleged rigging. “The other day, I demanded that the chief election commissioner should immediately decide on the constituencies where we have raised objections,” he said, calling for an investigation “based on fact and evidence”. He asked if the party did not have the right to approach the relevant forum over the matter, stressing that “only the people of Pakistan and Kashmir can be judges of the issue”. He also objected to statements by the PML-N leadership advising PPP to “move on”, raising alarm that PPP’s “legitimate grievances” were not being taken into account. The PPP leader then went on to show “video evidence” of the alleged rigging. “In this video in LA-12, a person can be seen picking up ballot papers and setting them on fire, along with 100-150 people who were led by the PML-N candidate,” the leader claimed. At this, Ashraf said he had brought the incident to the AJK Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan’s attention and asked: “It has been more than 48 hours since we brought this to your notice, but has there been any action taken against this person?” He continued: “How are you telling us to be brave and move on as the elections are when there are still two phases left?” He warned of serious repercussions given the lack of accountability for such conduct. The PPP leader then went on to highlight discrepancies in the results from some of the polling stations in the Mirpur division. “In polling station no.15 in LA-12, the total registered votes were 785, and the PML-N candidates secured 639 votes while our candidate got 12 votes and yet the results show that total votes were cast.” He pointed out that the polling station was in Charhoi, where he claimed at least 25pc of the people lived abroad and went on to question how every registered voter could have shown up. He noted that some of the polling stations had voter turnout of up to 99pc. At this, he remarked: “This can only happen when you are sitting down and stamping the ballot papers yourself”. “This is the story of the injustice I wanted to tell you,” he said, urging PML-N leadership to go to AJK and speak to the people. He warned: “If we sweep everything under the rug, then people are going to lose their faith in the election process.” Ashraf called on the AJK chief justice to pay attention to the issue, questioning how the total turnout could have jumped to such a significant extent in AJK. “You have ensured the PPP was defeated, and you have done a lot of planning [..], but when you pull such a move, there is always a trace,” he said. He called on AJK Chief Election Commissioner retired Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal to make a decision. “This is the third day, and you should have stopped the process when our complaints started coming in,” he said. Azma tells PPP to be ‘ashamed’; Sharjeel accuses PML-N of ‘dictator mindset’ Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon and Punjab’s Information Minister Azma Bokhari traded barbs as well, with Bokhari telling PPP to be “ashamed” of its performance in Sindh while Memon, in response, accused the PML-N of governing Punjab with a “dictator mindset” and through a “fake mandate”. Addressing a press conference, Bokhari criticised the PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, saying that Bilawal was trying to “imitate someone” without naming them. “The PML-N leadership never used abusive language nor targeted anyone whenever they addressed a gathering. They only talked about their progress, especially the work CM Maryam has done in the last 18 months,” she emphasised. During her address, Azma questioned, “Why was Karachi, Sindh’s provincial capital, at the mercy of the tanker mafia? Why does a big city like Karachi have no transport system while Punjab was running 1100 buses? Why was trash not being picked up from the roads of Karachi?” she asked. “No leader from PPP can answer these questions.” She also presented a progress report of the development work carried out in Punjab by the PML-N government, stating that in comparison, the PPP should be “ashamed” of its performance in Sindh in the last 18 years. In response to Bokhari, Memon accused the PML-N of coming into power through rigging in the 2024 General Election and said that the party intended to assume power in AJK in the same way. He said that the PPP formed a coalition with PML-N after the elections for the sake of the parliamentary process. “This is not a lie or an accusation, but the PML-N came into power through a fake mandate; even children of Pakistan know this,” he stated. He said that Mirpur is called the second United Kingdom because half of its population lives in different cities of the country. “In Yaseen Sahab’s constituency, there were only 20 polling stations, but the PML-N took up to 99.4pc votes,” he claimed, questioning how it was possible. “The PPP in any situation will not tolerate exploitation of the people of AJK. The PML-N is conspiring to steal the mandate of Kashmir’s people; however, they will not be able to,” he said. He said in another constituency, 110pc votes were cast — more than the total votes registered in the polling station — and demanded the AJK Election Commission take notice of this immediately. Memon further demanded re-polling in the constituencies where PPP had reservations. He further criticised Punjab CM, stating that the PML-N was ruling Punjab with “a dictator’s mindset”. Memon also recalled the case of Hum News’s journalist Khurram Iqbal, who, he claimed, had been “arrested and tortured” for tweeting about Maryam. The senior minister said that no television channel could run a ticker about the aftermath of rain in Punjab, fearing they may lose government advertising. Additional input from Tariq Naqash

items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca clôture dans le rouge
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a terminé dans le rouge mercredi, son indice principal, le MASI, cédant 0,34% à 17.739,77 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a diminué de 0,3% à 1.307,76 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, a reculé de 0,32% à 1.268,86 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, qui reflète la performance des petites et moyennes capitalisations, a baissé de 0,26% à 1.755,4 pts. Au volet international, le FTSE CSE Morocco 15 Index et le FTSE CSE Morocco All-Liquid ont clôturé sur des pertes respectives de 0,16% à 17.033,75 pts et de 0,25% à 15.287,02 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Sylviculture et papier » (-1,85%), « Assurances » (-1,52%) et « Société de financement et autres activités financières » (-1,34%) ont accusé les plus fortes baisses. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Boissons » (+2,51%), « Participation et promotion immobilières » (+0,71%) et « Télécommunications » (+0,33%) ont signé les meilleures performances. Les échanges ont dépassé 165,26 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés sur le marché central « Actions » dominés par les transactions sur T2S Group Holding (58,75 MDH), Jet Contractors (13,61 MDH) et Itissalat Al-Maghrib (11,97 MDH). La capitalisation boursière a avoisiné 1.025 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes baisses ont été affichées par Wafa Assurance (-2,83% à 5.150 DH), Bank of Africa (-2,58% à 185,1 DH), Mutandis (-2,54% à 226,1 DH), Cash Plus (-2,37% à 235,3 DH) et BMCI (-2,32% à 590 DH). En revanche, Zellidja (+5,79% à 243 DH), M2M Group (+5,47% à 384 DH), Société des Boissons du Maroc (+3,24% à 2.168 DH), AFMA (+2,36% à 1.260 DH) et Rebab Company (+2,22% à 90,04 DH) ont enregistré les plus fortes hausses. The post La Bourse de Casablanca clôture dans le rouge appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: SMT Ghana donates braille sheets, food items to Akropong School for the Blind
items.description: Government-assisted special school, the Akropong School for the Blind in the Eastern Region has received a donation of braille sheets and bags of rice from SMT Ghana to support teaching, learning and student welfare. The donation forms part of the company’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative aimed at promoting inclusive education and supporting vulnerable communities. According to SMT Ghana, the gesture reflects its corporate values of caring, daring and sharing by creating opportunities and making a positive impact beyond its business operations. The company’s Managing Director, Amaury Lescaux, led the delegation to the school. He was accompanied by Finance Director Afia Owusu Ansah, Aftersales Mining Director Maxwell Mokgolomotho, and Marketing and Communication Director Hilda Peasah. The SMT Ghana team was welcomed by the school’s management, staff, students and members of its donation committee. During the visit, the Girls’ Prefect demonstrated how visually impaired students read and write using braille paper, a slate and a stylus. Members of the delegation also had the opportunity to write in braille, giving them first-hand experience of the learning process for students with visual impairments. Presenting the items, Mr. Lescaux said education remains one of the most effective tools for transforming lives and should be accessible to every child. “At SMT Ghana, we believe that education is a powerful tool for transforming lives and should be accessible to every child. We are honoured to support the Akropong School for the Blind with learning materials and food supplies that will contribute to the students’ education and well-being,” he said. He also shared the story of Hakim Arezki, a French blind football (Cécifoot) player of Algerian origin, who overcame the loss of his sight to become an international athlete, describing his journey as evidence that disability should not limit one’s aspirations. Receiving the donation on behalf of the school, members of the school’s donation committee, Mr. Joseph Sowuh and Mr. Maxwell Asante Oware, expressed gratitude to SMT Ghana for the support. They said the braille sheets would significantly improve teaching and learning by providing students with essential learning materials, while the bags of rice would strengthen the school’s feeding programme and contribute to the students’ overall welfare. The committee described the donation as a demonstration of SMT Ghana’s commitment to inclusivity and social responsibility and appealed to other corporate organisations and individuals to emulate the gesture by supporting institutions that provide education and care for persons with disabilities.

items.title: Transplantation rénale au CHU de Tengandogo : Le Gouvernement salue la prouesse des équipes sanitaires
items.description: Une délégation gouvernementale composée du Ministre de l'Enseignement Supérieur, de la Recherche et de l'Innovation le camarade Pr Adjima THIOMBIANO et du Ministre de la santé, le camarade Dr Robert Lucien Jean Claude KARGOUGOU, était dans les locaux du Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Tengandogo (CHUT), ce mercredi 29 juillet 2026. Elle est allée rendre une visite et réconforter les patients bénéficiaires de la Transplantation rénale et féliciter les équipes sanitaires pour les prouesses réalisées dans cette opération délicate. La délégation ministérielle s'est d'abord rendue dans les salles de réanimation et d'hospitalisation où elle a rendu visite aux patients bénéficiaires de la transplantation rénale et leur apporter du réconfort. Dans ces salles, les ministres ont trouvé avec satisfaction, des patients sur le point de recouvrer progressivement la santé après l’opération. « Nous sommes très contents de vous voir aujourd'hui avec un beau sourire, nous vous souhaitons un prompt rétablissement », s’est adressé le Pr Adjima THIOMBIANO a un des patients qui venait d'être réanimé à l'issue d'une transplantation rénale. Très ému par cette visite, le patient a remercié la délégation pour cette visite qui donne du réconfort. Un autre patient, qui a donné un de ses reins et interné dans une salle d’hospitalisation, a également reçu la visite des membres du Gouvernement. Lui également est satisfait de la visite des ministres « nous apprécions cette visite des membres du Gouvernement, nous pouvons vous assurer que les médecins font bien leur travail ». A l'issue de la visite, les membres du Gouvernement ont tenu à saluer et féliciter les équipes à l'œuvre pour leur professionnalisme et leur patriotisme. «Nous sommes fiers de vous. Bravo pour tout ce que vous faites », a lancé le Pr Adjima THIOMBIANO à l’équipe en charge de ces patients avant de les inviter à plus d’engagement et de patriotisme car « les gens qui sont entre vos mains comptent sur vous pour vivre ». « Nous avons trouvé des équipes très engagées qui mettent le cœur à la tâche. Nous avons trouvé également des malades qui recouvrent parfaitement leur santé. Ce qui montre que c'est une opération réussie », a déclaré le ministre. » La délégation repart rassurée que la vision du Chef de l'État en matière de santé, à savoir assurer la souveraineté sanitaire dans notre pays, est sur le point de se réaliser. « Nous avons constaté l'effectivité de cette transplantation rénale qui montre véritablement une prouesse non seulement des équipes mais du système de santé dans son ensemble et vient consolider la vision du gouvernement qui était de faire bénéficier ces populations, des soins de santé avec des équipes endogènes. Donc nous repartons vraiment très satisfaits et très confiants que nous avons de l’expertise de haute facture pour prendre en charge de telles opérations », a conclu le Pr Adjima THIOMBIANO. Pour rendre cette opération possible, le Gouvernement burkinabè, sous la houlette du camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORE, Président du Faso, Chef de l’Etat a consenti des investissements conséquents. Le ministre chargé de l’enseignement a saisi cette occasion pour saluer le patriotisme de tous les burkinabè qui ont accepté de contribuer de façon volontaire au Fonds de Soutien Patriotique (FSP), afin de permettre au Gouvernement de mettre en place ce dispositif. Toute chose qui permettra à notre système sanitaire de disposer d’une expertise solide et de gagner la bataille pour la souveraineté sanitaire dans notre pays. DCRP-MESRI
